```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(targets)
library(ggplot2)
library(extrafont)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggrepel)

combinedTables <- tar_read(combinedTables, store = "store_visualize")

source("R/Visualization_PlotFunctions.R")

# extrafont::font_import()
extrafont::loadfonts()


timeData <- combinedTables$PrimaryTable
timeData$formattedName <- paste(timeData$formattedName, "\n")

totalData <- combinedTables$`PrimaryTable_2025-2051`
totalData$formattedName <- paste(totalData$formattedName, "\n")


stageData <- combinedTables$StageDist
stageData$formattedName <- paste(stageData$formattedName, "\n")

timeData_BreastDouble <- timeData
timeData_BreastDouble$Total_Screens[timeData$cancertype == "Breast"] <- timeData_BreastDouble$Total_Screens[timeData$cancertype == "Breast"] * 2

participationData <- combinedTables$Participation

```

# Cancer Type Specific Scenarios

 - Main results: Lung and Colorectal cancer seem to benefit from MCED (at high participation), however, it is far less effective with breast cancer
 - MCED does not work well until it surpasses ~60% participation
 - Overall interpretation: MCED is best suited to cancer types with insufficient screening, or when the tests have worse sensitivity/sensitivity. Lung cancer shows that underscreened types benefit, but well-screened types like breast will see a worsening of outcomes.



## Total Screens (Calibration)


```{r,fig.width=24,fig.height=12}

MCEDScreenNum <- totalData

MCEDScreenNum$Total_Screens[MCEDScreenNum$cancertype == "Breast" & MCEDScreenNum$testType %in% c("Galleri", "CancerSeek")] <- MCEDScreenNum$Total_Screens[MCEDScreenNum$cancertype == "Breast" & MCEDScreenNum$testType %in% c("Galleri", "CancerSeek")] * 2

visualizeTotals(MCEDScreenNum %>% filter(sce %in% scenariosToVisualize), "Total_Screens", "Number of Total Screens (2025-2051)", "Number of Cancer Screens (Breast MCED Doubled)")

```

## Efficiency Frontier


```{r,fig.width=16,fig.height=14}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

efficiencyPlots <- list()

for (type in c("Breast", "Colorectal", "Lung", "Combined")) {
  efficiencyPlots[type] <- list(visualizeFrontier(
    combinedTables$`PrimaryTable_2025-2051` %>%
      filter(testType != "NonMCED"),
    type
  ))
}
print(ggarrange(plotlist = efficiencyPlots, common.legend = TRUE))


```

- Breast does not seem to benefit from MCED at all
- Otherwise, several scenarios lead to cost efficiency when person years are the main metric examined

## Breast


```{r,fig.width=16,fig.height=14}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
visualizeSpecificCancerType(totalData %>% filter(sce %in% scenariosToVisualize), "Breast")

```


- The selected MCED scenarios generally lead to worse performance (fewer detected cases, more deaths, more cost)
- Overall: MCED never works well for breast


## Colorectal


```{r,fig.width=16,fig.height=14}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
visualizeSpecificCancerType(totalData %>% filter(sce %in% scenariosToVisualize), "Colorectal")

```

- Galleri with 90% participation is the only MCED scenario that results in fewer cancer deaths.
- It appears in terms of sensitivity, Galleri is better than FIT, and CancerSEEK is worse.
- Overall: MCED only works well for colorectal if it is Galleri and high participation

## Lung


```{r,fig.width=16,fig.height=14}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
visualizeSpecificCancerType(totalData %>% filter(sce %in% scenariosToVisualize), "Lung")

```

- Beside the NonMCED scenarios, 90% Galleri leads to the lowest increase in cost per additional detection. However, CancerSeek leads to the lowest increase in cost per death averted.
- Overall: MCED always helps with lung (largely due to lack of existing screening)

## Combined


```{r,fig.width=16,fig.height=14}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
visualizeSpecificCancerType(totalData %>% filter(sce %in% scenariosToVisualize), "Combined")

```

- Beside the NonMCED scenario, CancerSeek 90% leads to the lowest increase in cost per additional detection (among scenarios that increase detections)


## Linear Modelling

```{r,fig.width=16,fig.height=14}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

linearPlots <- list()

for (testType in c("Galleri", "CancerSeek", "NonMCED")) {
  linearPlots[testType] <- list(visualizeLinearModel(combinedTables, testType, "Person_years", "participation"))
}
print(ggarrange(plotlist = linearPlots, common.legend = TRUE, nrow = 3, ncol = 1))

```
